# Running the Design Loop {#sec-running-the-loop}

::: {.epigraph}
> *"Beware of bugs in the above code; I have only proved it correct, not tried it."*
>
> — Donald E. Knuth, *Notes on the van Emde Boas Construction of Priority Deques* (1977) [@Knuth1977PriorityDeques]
:::

::: {.column-margin}
**Author's Note:** Donald E. Knuth separated reasoning about code from the
evidence that comes from running it. An architecture study needs the same
discipline. A declared comparison, plausible teaching fixture, or carefully
reasoned plan does not become execution evidence until the tools run and the
returned artifacts are retained. The prospective cache record and executed
array record in this chapter therefore support different conclusions.
:::

::: {.callout-crux}
What can an architect conclude when the prospective Lighthouse cache study
cannot run, and what can a separate executed array study establish?
:::

Running a design loop means carrying a fixed architecture question through
candidate selection, tool execution, measurement, interpretation, and a
supported stopping decision. This chapter makes that sequence concrete with
two records that reach different stopping points. They teach different parts
of the work. They are not combined into one end-to-end result.

The first record follows the Lighthouse goal for a low-power, 64-bit
RISC-V-based compute subsystem for a real-time mobile extended reality (XR)
workload. We call it the Lighthouse cache study. It narrows that system goal to
one pre-RTL cache-capacity decision. The record is prospective. It specifies
the comparison and exposes the missing work that must be completed before any
candidate can run.

The Lighthouse cache study never reaches execution or produces a Lighthouse
result. The cache materials include author-constructed examples of fields that
an execution record could contain. They are teaching records, not measurements
from a cache run. The larger cache candidates remain unevaluated, the baseline
remains unrerun, and the pre-RTL decision remains open.

The second record is a separate [retained systolic-array
study](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/tree/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study),
with retained inputs and SCALE-Sim outputs. Its twelve simulator evaluation
events show what becomes possible after execution. The record supports a local
comparison, exposes a failed explanation and missing evidence, and reaches a
limited technical stop. It is not a Lighthouse study. It cannot complete the
cache record, validate the 3\ W subsystem target, or stand in for the Lighthouse
system.

::: {.callout-learning-objectives}
After reading this chapter, you can:

- Trace an architecture question through fixed state, execution, returned
  measurements, interpretation, and a supported stop.
- Distinguish a prospective study and teaching fixtures from retained execution
  evidence.
- Separate the architecture outcome, method contribution, mechanism result,
  and next action supported by a run.
- Use ties, failed explanations, omitted metrics, and provenance gaps to define
  a better follow-up study.

:::

## Preparing the Lighthouse Cache Study for Execution

The cache study first defines the architecture decision. Until the candidates,
controlled design fields, checks, and permitted conclusion are clear, a runnable
tool path has no well-defined comparison to execute. The study then asks what
must exist to run that comparison. Its declaration exposes the remaining work
without manufacturing a cache result.

### The Decision and Fixed State

The Lighthouse cache study begins with one architecture decision rather than
an AI method. The system goal is the 3\ W XR compute subsystem introduced in
@sec-moonshot. The local question asks which, if either, of two larger L2
capacities should advance to RTL evaluation against the current smaller
capacity. The comparison holds the rest of the architecture, workload, software,
and planned tool path fixed so that a capacity change is the intended cause of
any measured difference.

The comparison contains a 2\ MiB baseline, a 3\ MiB candidate, and a 4\ MiB
candidate. These capacities identify objects in the prospective study. They
are not retained cache configurations, generated instances, or measured
artifacts in this repository.

Capacity is the only swept architecture field, with specification choices of
2, 3, and 4\ MiB. That does not mean every request value remains identical.
A larger capacity may require a different set count, bank count, or SRAM macro
composition. Before dispatch, the study needs a rule that derives those values
while holding associativity, line size, indexing, replacement, miss status
holding register (MSHR) count, ports, hit-latency allocation, and process,
voltage, and temperature (PVT) assumptions fixed. The repository contains
neither that derivation rule nor the bound values for the controlled cache and
PVT fields, so the comparison cannot yet run.

The fixed state also covers the network-on-chip and memory-system
configurations, the 2\ GHz microarchitecture, compiler and runtime, RISC-V
software image, and workload snapshot with stable frame identifiers and
boundaries. The planned tool path combines an SRAM model with cycle-level
simulation, cache modeling, and power modeling. The repository does not yet
bind those roles to executable tools and retained measurement paths.

The architecture claim is that a larger L2 could reduce 99th-percentile frame
time by removing capacity misses while satisfying the declared power, area,
access-time, functional, and coherence checks. A reduction in misses alone
would not establish the claim. The matched frame observations would have to
show that the reduction reaches the tail-latency outcome under the fixed
workload and software state.

The legal set contains only the baseline and two alternatives. The study
therefore selects direct evaluation in @sec-methods-generation-prediction-optimization.
It adds no generator, predictor, optimizer, or learned search method. The SRAM
model belongs to the declared tool path rather than serving as a newly selected
AI component. With no added method, the cache study has no AI-contribution claim
to test. Direct evaluation is the smallest approach that could answer the
declared architecture question if the tool path existed.

The intended result is also narrow. The study could recommend at most one
capacity for a later RTL study. It could not authorize implementation,
signoff, tapeout, or a product commitment. Cache policy, prefetching,
coherence, network-on-chip changes, compiler changes, software scheduling,
full floorplanning, thermal signoff, resistive voltage-drop review, security,
reliability, and product cost remain outside the study.

### The Run Declaration and Remaining Work

Before any candidate can run, the study must turn each capacity into a controlled
request, bind a path that returns measurements and failures, and state when work
stops and what result may advance. The declaration groups this work as candidate
definition, executable path and returns, and stopping and decision fields.
Together they distinguish the candidates, fixed state, checks, budgets, and tool
responsibilities that must be bound before execution. None of these declarations
is an executed request (@tbl-cache-run-declaration).

| **Run field** | **Declared Lighthouse cache study work** |
| --- | --- |
| **Candidate requests** | Prepare one complete request to the SRAM model under the declared PVT conditions for the 2\ MiB baseline, 3\ MiB candidate, and 4\ MiB candidate. Treat `l2.capacity` as the only swept architecture field. Hold associativity, line size, indexing, replacement, MSHR count, ports, hit-latency allocation, and PVT fixed. A prospectively bound rule may derive set count, bank count, geometry, modeled periphery, and SRAM macro composition from capacity. Retain every controlled and derived value with the SRAM-model and technology identities. The repository contains no such bindings, so these requests are unfinished. |
| **Cycle-level requests** | Rerun the 2\ MiB baseline and run eligible candidates through the cycle-level simulator with the cache and power models while holding the declared XR workload snapshot, software image, and other hardware and software identities fixed. |
| **Dispatch condition** | No request is eligible until the controlled policy fields and all capacity-derived set, bank, geometry, periphery, and macro choices are bound. A cycle-level request is then eligible only when `(return_complete == true) && (schema_valid == true) && (area_mm2 <= 1.5) && (access_time_ns <= 2.5)`. This condition authorizes a request. It does not by itself validate a measurement or reject an architecture candidate. |
| **Required returns** | Retain SRAM area, access time, cache-local energy and leakage, matched frame records and frame-time inputs, 99th-percentile frame time, cache misses by classification, subsystem dynamic plus leakage power, tool and model identities, translated inputs, warnings, failures, hashes, lineage, and accounting records for queue and run time, compute use, license and tool use, retained storage, and human setup and review. The procedure that produces these cost records is not yet defined. |
| **Checks** | Require identical ISA-visible outputs for the declared tests, the same functional regression suite for every capacity, no failure from the simulator's coherence-invariant checks, modeled subsystem dynamic plus leakage power at or below 3\ W, cache macro area at or below 1.5\ mm^2^, modeled access time at or below 2.5\ ns, and an uncertainty-qualified frame-time comparison against the rerun baseline. Thermal and IR-drop review remain independent later requirements. |
| **Failure handling** | Refuse an invalid request before invocation. Keep timeouts, cancellations, infrastructure failures, stale state, missing output, and parser failures distinct. An authorized retry must link to its parent, consume the cycle-level budget, and begin from regenerated clean state without changing the candidate. |
| **Budget** | Allow three SRAM evaluations and at most four cycle-level executions in total, including infrastructure reruns. No RTL synthesis or physical signoff is included. Before execution, define how the study accounts for queue and run time, compute use, license and tool use, retained storage, and human setup and review, including the records or tool returns that supply each cost. This accounting procedure is unfinished. |
| **Stopping** | Stop an attempt when its queue-wait or run-time deadline expires. Stop the study when the intended decision is resolved, all eligible capacities are exhausted, the cycle-level budget is spent, the absolute deadline expires, a required input or tool remains unavailable, or no alternative passes the SRAM limits. The numeric queue-wait, run-time, and absolute deadlines remain undefined pre-execution work and block dispatch. |
| **Decision** | The direction rule requires an uncertainty-qualified frame-time improvement greater than zero. Before execution, define the estimator, interval or confidence procedure, and any additional practical margin prospectively. Once those are fixed, recommend at most one capacity for later RTL evaluation only when its required checks pass and its qualified comparison against the rerun baseline shows the declared improvement. |

: **The declaration exposes what blocks the cache run.** It identifies the
intended requests, returns, checks, call-count limits, and decision while
leaving cache-policy and derived-structure bindings, the statistical procedure,
cost accounting, numeric deadlines, and the executable measurement path
unfinished.
{#tbl-cache-run-declaration tbl-colwidths="[22,78]"}

The declaration fixes the required direction but not the procedure for judging
it. Baseline latency minus candidate latency must be qualified above zero. The
estimator, interval or confidence procedure, and any practical margin must be
fixed before dispatch so that the team cannot choose an interpretation after
seeing the returns. The call-count limits also leave the cost procedure and
numeric queue-wait, run-time, and absolute deadlines unfinished. Those gaps
block dispatch even though the candidate count is known.

All declared capacities and serialized values use mebibytes (MiB), where
1\ MiB is $2^{20}$ bytes [@NISTBinaryPrefixes]. The three capacity labels remain
stable specification names. An executable request must carry the declared MiB
token and byte count into every dependent request before comparison begins.

Nothing in @tbl-cache-run-declaration was materialized or executed for this
book. No functional regression, coherence check, tail-latency comparison,
power check, area check, access-time check, thermal review, or IR-drop review
produced cache evidence.

## Why the Lighthouse Cache Study Stops Before Execution

A missing implementation path does not erase the study definition, but it limits
what an architect can conclude. The architect must first inspect what was retained.
Only then can the architect state what that material supports about the unresolved
decision and name the prerequisites for any new execution. That sequence prevents
a detailed plan from being mistaken for an experiment.

### What the Repository Retains

The cache material preserves two kinds of prospective evidence but nothing from
an actual run. Specification identities state what a study intends to compare,
while author-constructed teaching records show what an execution record could
look like. Executed evidence would require retained requests, outputs, statuses,
and lineage from an actual run. As @tbl-cache-evidence-inventory shows, the
repository retains the first two classes and no executed cache evidence.

| **Retained item** | **Evidence class** | **What it supports** | **What remains absent** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lighthouse cache study, current design revision, controlled-state identities, and the three cache candidates | Specification identity | The cache question, comparator, intended controlled state, permitted capacity change, required measurements, call-count limits, stopping categories, and intended pre-RTL decision. | Bound policy fields, capacity-derived cache structure, retained candidate artifacts, executable requests, runs, measurements, and a cache disposition. |
| Run declaration and its declared tool roles | Specification identity | The intended request translation, dispatch condition, return schema, failure handling, call-count limits, and tool responsibilities. | Numeric deadlines, a cost-accounting procedure, bound executables, wrapper and parser versions, exact inputs, host state, commands, logs, outputs, and realized cost. |
| Constructed SRAM and simulator entries plus a design-loop card that summarizes the proposed question, state, returns, checks, and decision | Author-constructed teaching fixture | Illustrative area, access-time, power, failure, return, and summary fields that a study record might retain. | Terminal and parser status, exact requests, raw artifacts, state identities, dispatch evidence, lineage, realized cost, and any measured cache result. |
| Retained cache execution package | Executed evidence | None. No such package is present. | Candidate artifacts, tool requests, raw outputs, parsed measurements, hashes, lineage, costs, qualified comparisons, and a decision record. |

: **The repository retains a cache specification and teaching fixtures, not a
cache experiment.** Similar-looking identifiers across chapters do not convert
constructed entries into executed evidence. {#tbl-cache-evidence-inventory tbl-colwidths="[22,18,28,32]"}

The constructed values keep missing fields visible. They do not show that a
request ran or that any candidate was measured, rejected, or advanced. The
absent 4\ MiB request does not prove that a dispatch check rejected that
candidate. The illustrative 3\ MiB values do not establish feasibility,
performance, or compliance with the 3\ W limit, and the baseline entry does not
show that the 2\ MiB baseline was rerun under matched conditions. The capacities
and tool roles remain parts of the specification rather than names of retained
cache artifacts.

### Four Judgments and the Next Action

Even without execution, the architect must report separately what happened to
the architecture decision, method contribution, proposed mechanism, and why the
study stopped. This lecture formally proposes the four judgments in
@tbl-cache-judgments as a community standard taxonomy for evaluating future AI-architecture
literature. Because this standard separates the architecture outcome from the AI contribution, mechanism,
and stopping condition, it prevents conflating a successful tool demonstration
with a viable silicon breakthrough. The template keeps local conclusions distinct. It does
not replace the complete-system evaluation map in @sec-evaluating-agentic-architect, which
compares complete workflows across tasks, costs, and conditions.

| **Judgment** | **Cache conclusion** | **Evidence boundary** |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Architecture outcome** | Unresolved. No capacity advances, and none is rejected. | No retained cache candidate was executed, the baseline was not rerun, and no required comparison was qualified. |
| **AI contribution** | Not tested. | Direct evaluation with no added learned method was the declared approach. No AI-versus-conventional comparison exists. |
| **Mechanism** | Untested. | No retained miss classifications or matched frame observations test whether reduced capacity misses change 99th-percentile frame time. |
| **Stopping** | Stop before execution because the implementation, measurement, and dispatch prerequisites are unavailable. | The declared budget was not consumed. If the cache decision remains worth pursuing, a new run requires bound policy and derived cache choices, numeric deadlines, a cost-accounting procedure, candidate artifacts, tool bindings, request translation, and an executable measurement path. Deferral, cancellation, or reformulation remain legitimate. |

: **The cache decision remains open for four different reasons.** Missing
execution leaves the architecture outcome unresolved, the declared no-added-method
choice leaves AI contribution untested, missing observations leave the mechanism
untested, and absent execution prerequisites fix the stopping point. {#tbl-cache-judgments tbl-colwidths="[18,34,48]"}

The stop belongs before execution. It is not budget exhaustion, a failed
candidate, or a no-change architecture result, and it authorizes none of the
three capacities for RTL work. If the cache decision remains worth pursuing,
the missing bindings, procedures, artifacts, and executable measurement path
must be supplied in a new run. Deferral, cancellation, or reformulation are
also supported responses.

## A Separate Executed Array Study {#sec-executed-scale-study}

The cache record shows where a prospective study must stop before execution.
The separate systolic-array record begins with measurements returned by
actual tools. Those measurements do not create one overall verdict. An
architect must interpret them against the frozen question, then state the
architecture outcome, study-local AI contribution, mechanism result, and next
action separately.

### The Frozen Array Comparison

The retained systolic-array study lives in the [tagged v0.1.7
package](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/tree/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study)
under the name `arch2_scale_ai_study_v1`. The package preserves its
preregistration, model and execution provenance, results, and manifest.
Preregistration fixes the question, comparison, and interpretation rules before
the tools return results, so an outcome cannot retroactively change the test
[@NosekEtAl2018Preregistration]. It freezes the legal array shapes, score,
budget, rejection checks, mechanism contrast, and decision boundary before
execution begins.

The study evaluates systolic-array shapes for three synthetic general matrix
multiplication (GEMM) layers. A GEMM multiplies an
$M \times K$ activation matrix by a $K \times N$ weight matrix to produce an
$M \times N$ output matrix. The three recorded $(M, N, K)$ dimension tuples
are 128 by 128 by 256, 64 by 192 by 128, and 32 by 128 by 192. The
local architecture purpose is to compare systolic-array geometries under one
fixed workload and simulator configuration. The layers are not traces from an
identified spatial-tracking pipeline or a complete XR application.

SCALE-Sim is a configurable cycle-accurate simulator for systolic accelerators.
Its published design supports several dataflows and system-analysis options
[@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3]. This study uses only a specific subset. It changes
array height and width under SCALE-Sim 3.0.0 with weight-stationary dataflow,
128\ KiB for each of the three SRAMs, and configured interface bandwidth values
of 64. Those choices come from the package's
[frozen preregistration](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/context/pre_registration.yaml)
and retained per-run configurations, not from the simulator paper.

Weight-stationary execution keeps weight tiles at processing elements while
activation values move through the array and partial sums accumulate, reducing
repeated weight movement [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3]. The retained study fixes a
1,024-processing-element legality limit, a 90,000-cycle cutoff, a mandatory 32
by 32 baseline, four simulator evaluation events per proposal arm, and four
shared mechanism-probe events. It also records an 800\ MHz clock for
optional derived latency. Every judgment here uses cycles rather than that
clock.

The fixed heuristic is the budget-matched method comparator for the frozen
study. Exhaustive enumeration would instead provide a full-space reference for
the fifteen-shape legal space, at greater simulator cost than either four-event
proposal arm. Its absence limits coverage, but it cannot be added
retroactively.

The local lower-is-better score is

$$
S = \frac{\text{total cycles}}
         {\text{average layer utilization}/100}.
$$

The runner computes this score from retained SCALE-Sim outputs. It is not a
physical measurement, an area-delay product, or a universal accelerator
metric. The runner sums the `Total Cycles` column and excludes the separate
prefetch-inclusive column. Average layer utilization is the arithmetic mean of
the three per-layer SCALE-Sim `Overall Util %` values, not `Compute Util %`, so
each layer has equal weight. The score does not explicitly price
processing-element count, area, or modeled memory traffic.

For the frozen decision rule, lower is better. A legal nonbaseline candidate
clears the 1 percent support margin when
$S_{\text{candidate}} \leq 0.99 \times S_{32\times32}$; equality at this
threshold passes.

The runner constructs both arms from the same three-row CSV workload, which
records a layer name and the M, N, and K dimensions for each dense GEMM. Array
rows and columns come only from the set 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128, and their product
must not exceed 1,024 processing elements. The runner inserts the mandatory 32
by 32 baseline, then holds the workload, layout, SCALE-Sim configuration,
dataflow, SRAM capacities, bandwidth fields, deadline, checks, and local score
fixed for every candidate.

The model's permitted role is equally narrow. It may return three unique legal
nonbaseline shapes and a mechanism hypothesis. It cannot invoke SCALE-Sim,
waive a check, choose the recommendation, or make the architecture decision.
The deterministic heuristic excludes the baseline and orders every legal
shape first by decreasing processing-element count, then by the absolute
log2 distance between the shape's columns-to-rows ratio and the aggregate
workload N-to-M ratio, and finally by increasing row count and column count.
It selects the first three shapes in that order.

The inserted baseline gives each proposal arm four simulator events. This is
equal simulator-event allocation, not equal total effort. The study does not
equate those events with model inference, prompt development, heuristic
construction, human setup, or review cost.

### The Retained Chronology

The frozen comparison defines what the tools are allowed to answer. The
chronology now shows what actually ran. One setup failure precedes a valid
model call and twelve successful simulator evaluation records. As
@fig-array-study-workflow shows, the schema failure returns to repair and
revalidation before any candidate reaches simulation. The resulting record
supports four separate judgments rather than treating a simulator return as an
architecture decision.

![**One retained record supports four separate judgments.** The array study freezes its question, legal space, score, budget, and checks before proposal selection. A schema failure returns to repair and revalidation before execution. The interpreted record then supports distinct judgments about the architecture outcome, study-local AI contribution, proposed mechanism, and stopping point.](images/ch8_design_loop_workflow){#fig-array-study-workflow width="100%" fig-alt="An architecture workflow freezes a plan and validates a proposal schema before selecting candidates, checking legality, and executing simulator runs. A failed schema returns through repair and revalidation. One shared stem from the interpreted record then branches to four boxes for the architecture outcome, study-local AI contribution, mechanism status, and stopping judgment."}

The retained chronology in @tbl-array-chronology keeps the execution order,
available costs, and missing provenance visible rather than filling the gaps.

| **Recorded event** | **Action and return** | **Retained support and limit** |

No external timestamp or commit binding independently proves precedence. |
| **Rejected schema request, 18:21:00 UTC** | The response-format service rejects the original JSON Schema, the machine-readable contract for structured JSON output, before inference because two constant-string properties lack explicit types. No model output or usage is produced. | The old and new schema hashes and a prose error description are retained. The rejected schema body and service response are not retained, so semantic equivalence of the amendment cannot be independently checked. |

: **The array chronology records what happened and what is missing.** The
[preregistration](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/context/pre_registration.yaml),
[model provenance](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/model/provenance.json),
[execution provenance](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/execution_provenance.json),
and [study results](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/study_results.json)
record one schema setup failure before a valid model call, twelve completed
simulator events, and no authorized acceptance or rejection.
{#tbl-array-chronology tbl-colwidths="[20,40,40]"}

The response-format service rejects the schema before inference, so the record
treats the failure as request translation and interface validation. The
architecture question, legal shape set, score, and evaluation budget do not
change. The record treats the amendment as request repair within the study. Only
after repair and revalidation does the valid proposal call return candidates for
legality checking and simulation. The missing schema body and service response
prevent a reviewer from confirming that the amendment preserved the request's meaning.

The [model
provenance](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/model/provenance.json)
names OpenAI through Codex CLI 0.144.4 and the requested alias `gpt-5.4`. It
records 13,223 input tokens, including 1,920 cached tokens, and 1,446 output
tokens, including 516 reasoning tokens. Currency cost was not reported. The
exact hosted model revision and sampling identity[^fn-sampling-identity-c08]
were not exposed, so another call cannot be treated as reproduction of this
one.

[^fn-sampling-identity-c08]: **Sampling identity**: The retained model record lacks a seed, temperature, top-p, exact hosted revision, and serving state, so this book does not claim exact reproduction.

The retained prompt has a second provenance break. The preregistration and
model record name SHA-256 `ec12df200a134532...76fbca`, while the surviving
prompt copy hashes to `36e0167aa338c6b...6971`. The complete response survives,
but the exact context that produced it cannot be verified.

The simulator provenance records macOS 26.4 on arm64, Python 3.11.15,
`arch2_labs` 0.1.0, SCALE-Sim 3.0.0, and a local executable path. It does not
bind the historical runner to a repository commit, dependency lock,
container, or complete host state. The reference manifest covers the retained
reference-output tree, not the preregistration, prompt, model response,
provenance record, runner source, dependency lock, or repository commit as one
sealed identity.

Full-system simulation studies have shown that implementation,
configuration, and model choices can produce materially different results
[@GutierrezEtAl2014SourcesOfError]. That precedent explains why simulator
provenance matters here; it does not diagnose an error in this retained run or
identify which missing identity, if any, changed its result.

The retained array directory contains no independently preserved validation
receipt artifact. Without one, a reviewer cannot treat reference integrity,
replay, or focused tests as independently verified. The retained files and
current replay path remain inspectable, but replay would still share the
workload, runner, simulator, score, and assumptions of the recorded computation.
The executed record contains no study-local independent analytical, RTL, or
cross-simulator check. No analytical fold-count sanity check ran. A newly frozen
mechanism study could add that check as future work, but the mapping discussion
below is the author's interpretation of the tagged simulator implementation,
not executed evidence.

These provenance gaps limit replay and causal claims, but they do not erase the
retained simulator outputs. Those outputs can still answer the frozen local
comparison within the recorded workload, simulator configuration, score, and
checks.

### The Local Results

The model arm evaluates the mandatory baseline plus its three proposals. The
fixed aggregate-aspect-ratio heuristic evaluates the same baseline plus 16 by
64, 8 by 128, and 64 by 16. The two arms overlap on two nonbaseline shapes.
Including the repeated baseline, both arms receive four simulator evaluation
events. Matched sample budgets are useful for comparing architecture-search
methods, as ArchGym's equal-sample comparisons illustrate
[@KrishnanEtAl2023ArchGym]. In this retained study, however, the matched unit is
only the number of simulator events. It does not equalize simulator compute,
model inference, human setup, heuristic construction, prompt development,
workflow failures, review effort, or total cost.

Equal simulator-event budgets produce a tied best evaluated score in both
proposal arms. Repeated rows remain separate budget events, not independent
measurements (@tbl-array-results).

| **Arm** | **Shape and source** | **PE count (author-derived)** | **Cycles** | **Average layer utilization** | **Local score** | **Result within arm** |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Model | 32 by 32 baseline | `{python} f"{32 * 32:,}"` | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Model | 16 by 64 proposal | `{python} f"{16 * 64:,}"` | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Model | 8 by 128 proposal | `{python} f"{8 * 128:,}"` | 19,405 | 29.704% | 65,327.45 | Ranked worse |
| Model | 32 by 16 proposal | `{python} f"{32 * 16:,}"` | 25,277 | 45.438% | 55,629.61 | Ranked worse |
| Heuristic | 32 by 32 baseline | `{python} f"{32 * 32:,}"` | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Heuristic | 16 by 64 proposal | `{python} f"{16 * 64:,}"` | 13,917 | 41.196% | 33,782.40 | Tied best |
| Heuristic | 8 by 128 proposal | `{python} f"{8 * 128:,}"` | 19,405 | 29.704% | 65,327.45 | Ranked worse |
| Heuristic | 64 by 16 proposal | `{python} f"{64 * 16:,}"` | 17,757 | 32.294% | 54,985.25 | Ranked worse |

: **The two proposal arms tie under equal simulator-event budgets.** Neither
finds an evaluated nonbaseline shape that clears the recorded one-percent
margin over 32 by 32. The values come from the [retained study
results](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/study_results.json),
not silicon. PE counts are author-derived from rows times columns.
{#tbl-array-results tbl-colwidths="[10,19,12,10,16,13,20]"}

The 32 by 16 proposal contains `{python} f"{32 * 16:,}"` processing elements,
while 32 by 32, 16 by 64, 8 by 128, and 64 by 16 each contain
`{python} f"{32 * 32:,}"`. Shape and processing-element count therefore vary
together in the 32 by 16 comparison. A design with
`{python} f"{32 * 16:,}"` processing elements may have a different resource
tradeoff from the relevant shapes with `{python} f"{32 * 32:,}"` processing
elements, but this study measured no area or energy consequence of that
difference. The retained result remains a score-only local outcome.

The best evaluated nonbaseline, 16 by 64, exactly matches the baseline on
cycles, average layer utilization, and local score. It does not clear the
change margin. The 8 by 128, 32 by 16, and 64 by 16 results rank worse under
the frozen score. This is a no-change outcome for five unique evaluated
shapes. It is not evidence that 32 by 32 is optimal among all legal shapes.

The proposal ranking ties, while the mechanism test fails its declared reversal
(@fig-ai-study-result). These results answer different questions, so the tied
score cannot serve as support for the directional explanation.

The tie provides no study-local AI advantage over the fixed heuristic
under equal simulator-event budgets. It also provides no evidence of equal
capability, equal total cost, or parity with exhaustive enumeration, an expert
study, a solver, or another search method. One proposal call supplies no estimate
of variation or reliability for the model family.

The retained results establish equal cycles and average layer utilization for
32 by 32 and 16 by 64 under the frozen score, but they do not establish the
architectural cause of that equality. The following transposition probe tests
a separate mechanism hypothesis by comparing 16 by 64 with 64 by 16.

### The Failed Directional Explanation

The model predicted that 16 by 64 would beat 64 by 16 on the original workload
and that 64 by 16 would win after M and N were exchanged. The [retained study
results](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/study_results.json)
give original local scores of 33,782.40 and 54,985.25 and transposed scores of
23,530.65 and 25,458.11. The predicted reversal does not occur. The narrower
transposed gap does not rescue the explanation.

The surviving prompt copy also omits the mapping semantics needed to interpret
the contrast. The retained execution records identify SCALE-Sim 3.0.0 but no
dependency hash or source commit. The K-height, N-width, and M-temporal
interpretation here follows the tagged v3.0.0 implementation
[@ScaleSimProject2025V300Source]. Under SCALE-Sim's weight-stationary GEMM
mode, K maps across the array height, N maps across its width, and M advances
over time rather than occupying a spatial array dimension
(@fig-array-mapping). A fold count is the number of array-sized passes needed
to cover a mapped workload dimension, such as $\lceil K/\text{height}\rceil$
or $\lceil N/\text{width}\rceil$. Exchanging M and N changes the temporal
extent and the width-mapped dimension while leaving K unchanged. Mirroring 16
by 64 and 64 by 16 simultaneously changes both the N-fold count on width and
the K-fold count on height, so the probe does not isolate array orientation.

![**The retained contrast does not isolate array orientation.** In the tagged SCALE-Sim v3.0.0 implementation [@ScaleSimProject2025V300Source], weight-stationary GEMM maps K to array height and N to array width, while M streams through the array. Exchanging M and N leaves K unchanged, so the mirrored shapes change more than one fold count.](images/F8-array-mapping){#fig-array-mapping fig-alt="A GEMM workload feeds a resident weight tile of K by N, which maps onto wide 16 by 64 and tall 64 by 16 arrays. K maps over array height and N over array width. A dashed transpose connector notes that K is unchanged, so the mirrored pair changes more than one fold count."}

The directional prediction fails its declared test, but the contrast does not
establish a replacement mechanism. It does not show that orientation is
irrelevant. A new mechanism study would need a prompt with pinned mapping
semantics and a contrast that varies one relevant fold count at a time.

The retained report exposes a separate simulator-semantics limit. The
transposed 16 by 64 input config declares `Bandwidth = 64,64,64`, while the
exact [retained bandwidth
report](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/runs/probe_transposed_16x64/scalesim-results/probe_transposed_16x64/BANDWIDTH_REPORT.csv)
gives `Avg OFMAP DRAM BW` as 79.073 in one row. The record does not explain the
relationship between those fields. Their bandwidth semantics remain
unresolved, and the configured value is not evidence of a demonstrated
physical or shared-system limit. This issue neither explains nor rescues the
failed reversal.

The retained SCALE-Sim configuration and outputs establish none of the
physical properties that the Lighthouse decision needs. This run preserves no
energy, physical bandwidth, timing, power, area, thermal, or silicon result,
even though the broader SCALE-Sim v3 tool supports additional memory, energy,
and power analyses [@RajEtAl2025ScaleSimV3]. The configured bandwidth fields
and reported operand traffic do not describe a verified shared-system
interface. The synthetic workload and local array result cannot close the
cache decision, the 3\ W requirement, or the Lighthouse system.

## Coverage and Proxy Limits

The executed result is narrow even within its local array question. The legal
space is small and closed, with exactly fifteen shapes under the declared
dimension set and 1,024-processing-element limit.
The retained proposal-arm evaluations cover only five of the fifteen legal
shapes, leaving ten without an executed result (@tbl-array-shape-coverage).

| **Status** | **Exact legal shapes** | **Count** |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Evaluated as unique original-workload geometries | 8 by 128; 16 by 64; 32 by 16; 32 by 32; 64 by 16 | 5 |
| Not executed | 8 by 8; 8 by 16; 8 by 32; 8 by 64; 16 by 8; 16 by 16; 16 by 32; 32 by 8; 64 by 8; 128 by 8 | 10 |

: **Five evaluated geometries do not close a fifteen-shape space.** Repeated
arm events preserve the frozen budgets but add no new geometry. The ten other
legal shapes have no retained SCALE-Sim result. {#tbl-array-shape-coverage tbl-colwidths="[25,62,13]"}

For a newly frozen follow-up study, exhaustive enumeration would provide a
full-space reference by evaluating every legal shape under one fixed workload,
simulator configuration, score, and set of checks. It is not budget-matched to
the current four-event proposal arms. A follow-up must either budget its greater
simulator cost explicitly or use it only as a coverage baseline. The current
study did not perform that enumeration. No outcome for the ten unexecuted shapes
can be inferred, and enumeration cannot be added retroactively to claim that
the recorded model tied or beat the complete space.

The frozen score also omits a reported axis that could matter to a later
system decision. The 16 by 64 shape ties the baseline at 13,917 cycles and
41.196 percent average layer utilization, yet the [retained study
results](https://github.com/harvard-edge/arch2/blob/f5516e52e66243c2d753191e350a5cfac56c83af/labs/examples/ai_systolic_array_study/recorded/reference/study_results.json)
contain 409,726 modeled DRAM writes for 16 by 64 and 204,863 for 32 by 32. The
64 by 16 shape reports 102,400 modeled writes and fewer total modeled accesses
than the baseline while taking more cycles. These are simulator outputs, not
identified physical DRAM transactions or energy measurements.

The baseline dominates the shared 16 by 64 candidate on the two reported
quantities of cycles and modeled writes (@fig-proxy-mismatch). This post-run
observation exposes a proxy limitation. It does not change the frozen score,
establish physical memory energy, or authorize a different decision.

```{python}

Across cycles and modeled DRAM writes, the baseline dominates that candidate. This post-run observation does not change the frozen outcome or establish physical memory energy.

arm_runs = [r for r in result["evaluations"] if r["arm"] in {"model", "conventional"}]
```

A new enumeration study would need to freeze its decision quantities before
execution. It could retain the original local score for comparability, add a
separately justified memory-aware quantity, or replace the score. None of
those choices can rescore the retained executed study. The unresolved memory
axis is part of the reason that neither exhaustive coverage nor the current
local ranking alone would establish energy, power, or Lighthouse suitability.

The tied ranking, failed directional explanation, and omission of modeled
memory traffic from the frozen score change the next study. A follow-up should
budget a full-space reference separately, revise the metric prospectively
rather than rescore this record, and isolate one proposed mechanism at a
time.

## Two Stops and Their Next Actions

The Lighthouse cache path and the separate executed array study reach different
technical stopping points and support different next actions
(@tbl-lighthouse-return).

| **Record** | **Architecture outcome** | **AI contribution** | **Mechanism** | **Stopping and action** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Lighthouse cache path | Unresolved. No cache candidate was evaluated, rejected, or advanced. | Not tested because direct evaluation with no added learned method was selected. | Untested. No retained result connects capacity misses to 99th-percentile frame time. | Stop before execution because the cache implementation, measurement, and dispatch prerequisites are unavailable. If the decision remains worth pursuing, continuation requires a new fully retained run with the missing bindings, procedures, and artifacts. Deferral, cancellation, or reformulation remain legitimate. |
| Separate executed array study | No evaluated nonbaseline clears the local margin for five unique shapes. This is not an optimality result. | No study-local advantage is demonstrated over the fixed heuristic under equal simulator-event budgets. Equal total cost and method parity were not measured. | The directional reversal prediction fails, and no replacement explanation is established. | The machine-readable recommendation is to retain 32 by 32 for the evaluated set and stop the local technical search. No authorized acceptance or rejection was recorded. |

: **The two records stop at different technical boundaries.** The Lighthouse
cache path never executes, while the separate retained array study executes a
narrow simulator comparison for which no authorized acceptance or rejection
was recorded. They are not stages of one end-to-end Lighthouse run, and neither
result can close the other.
{#tbl-lighthouse-return tbl-colwidths="[19,22,20,18,21]"}

In the executed array case, each returned signal changes a different claim
and therefore a different next action. Some actions belong to the current
record, while others require a newly frozen study.

- **Tie.** The returned scores affect the claim that the model-guided proposals
  improve the local architecture result. They support no study-local advantage
  over the fixed heuristic under equal simulator-event budgets, so the current
  record retains 32 by 32 for the evaluated set. Testing a broader selection
  claim requires a newly frozen, separately budgeted full-space reference.
- **Failed mechanism.** The transposition results affect the directional
  explanation, not the measured ranking. They reject the predicted reversal
  without establishing a replacement mechanism. Isolating that mechanism
  requires a newly frozen study with pinned mapping semantics.
- **Omitted metric.** The modeled traffic counts expose a quantity absent from
  the frozen score. They do not change the current ranking or permit post-run
  rescoring. Any memory-aware decision quantity belongs in a newly frozen
  study.
- **Provenance gap.** The missing prompt identity and incomplete simulator
  provenance limit a reproduction claim. The current record remains usable
  within those limits. A new run must retain the exact prompt, model revision
  when available, runner revision, dependencies, commands, and complete
  outputs.
- **Pending authority.** The machine-readable technical recommendation retains
  32 by 32 for the evaluated set, but no authorized acceptance or rejection
  was recorded. The next action within the current record is review, not an
  architecture commitment.

The tie, failed mechanism, omitted metric, and provenance gap identify possible
follow-up studies. None ran as part of the retained execution, and each would
need a separately frozen comparison. Even those studies would not establish XR
behavior or the 3\ W system target because the retained configuration and
outputs lack the required system checks.

Both records leave the central system questions open. Neither retains an
identified XR workload trace or validates tail deadlines across deployed
conditions. Neither executes the compiler, runtime, RISC-V interface, host
cores, shared memory path, sensors, or display engine. Neither supplies a
complete verification plan or checks the full subsystem's function, security,
or reliability.

The physical questions also remain. No retained evidence closes timing,
routing, area, power delivery, the 3\ W subsystem budget, thermal behavior, or
silicon performance. The array reports contain modeled local traffic, but no
shared-memory contention or physical energy model connects that traffic to the
Lighthouse platform. The cache plan names some of these checks, but naming a
check is not running it.

## Open Questions

The chapter's unexecuted and executed records leave open four problems about
operating an AI-assisted architecture study: deciding whether the current
state supports execution, allocating scarce evaluation capacity, revising the
plan, and stopping at the last supported result. The records expose different
evidence boundaries and do not support claims beyond what each retains.

**Choosing the next architecture action.** An architect running a study must
choose whether to execute, repair, or reformulate and where to spend scarce
evaluation capacity.

- **How should an architect decide whether the next action should be execution,
  repair, or reformulation?** Retained study states with
  known missing or inconsistent prerequisites make action selection measurable
  through invalid dispatches, unnecessary repair or reformulation, and the cost
  of reaching a supported result. The difficult cases arise when individually
  plausible candidates, tools, measurements, and decision rules do not form a
  runnable comparison together.

- **How should a running study allocate limited simulation, implementation, and
  review capacity among its remaining candidates and checks?** Fixed,
  cheapest-first, and decision-aware allocations can be compared under the same
  total budget. The relevant outcomes are how often the architecture decision
  is resolved, how much work continues after the result is already determined,
  and how often an allocation misses the candidate or check that would change
  the supported conclusion.

**Replanning and stopping.** Failures and interim results may justify changing
the plan, but those changes cannot retroactively alter the comparison or
strengthen the last supported result.

Hyperband provides a precedent for allocating a divisible resource across
configurations and stopping weak configurations when intermediate fidelities
are meaningful [@LiEtAl2018Hyperband]. That transfer is conditional. Many RTL,
formal-verification, synthesis, and physical-design runs are indivisible, lack
a trustworthy intermediate fidelity, or cannot be discarded without losing
needed coverage. Hyperband therefore supplies an allocation idea, not evidence
that adaptive stopping fits this retained study or architecture tool runs in
general.

- **How can a running architecture study revise its experiment after failures
  or interim results without invalidating the comparison it reports?** Frozen
  and adaptive plans expose the tradeoff between responding to useful new
  information and steering later runs toward a favorable result. Outcome bias,
  candidate and condition coverage, and supported decision quality at matched
  tool budgets make that tradeoff visible.

- **When should a running architecture study stop, and what result should it
  retain?** A sound stopping rule must avoid both continued work after the
  architecture decision is settled and premature claims from incomplete
  evidence. Decision quality, extra tool and review cost, premature stops, and
  unsupported conclusions relative to a fixed-budget policy expose both
  failures.

## Conclusion

::: {.callout-design-principle title="Claim only what the checked record supports"}
Treat the checked record as the ceiling on every claim. Keep the plan, executed
artifact, qualified local result, tested mechanism, architecture outcome, AI
contribution, and stopping decision distinct. An unexecuted plan and a separate
local study cannot fill each other's evidence gaps. Blending those records
fabricates continuity and overstates both outcomes. A reviewer should be able
to trace each claim to retained execution and a suitable check. A new frozen
study may continue the work, while prior valid evidence remains historical
within its original scope rather than becoming automatic support for the new
claim.
:::

The Lighthouse cache study reaches a supported stop before execution. Its exact
candidate identities, controlled-state declarations, planned requests, required
returns, checks, call-count limits, and intended pre-RTL decision survive. Its
policy bindings, capacity-derived structure, numeric deadlines, cost-accounting
procedure, implementation path, and measurement path do not. The repository
therefore supports no cache measurement, candidate rejection, retry, dispatch,
return, cost, baseline comparison, AI-contribution result, mechanism result, or
architecture recommendation.

The separate array study reaches a different stop. It retains one schema
setup failure, one valid model response with provenance gaps, twelve SCALE-Sim
evaluation events, five unique evaluated shapes, a tie against a fixed
heuristic, a failed directional explanation, an omitted memory axis, and a
technical recommendation to retain 32 by 32 for the evaluated set and stop.
No authorized acceptance or rejection was recorded. The study does not
establish array optimality, equal total cost, method parity, physical
feasibility, or any full-system XR result.

Neither record produces a win claim. If the cache decision remains worth
pursuing, a new fully retained execution requires the missing cache bindings,
numeric deadlines, cost procedure, artifacts, and measurement path. Deferral,
cancellation, or reformulation remain legitimate. A broader array
candidate-selection claim would require a newly frozen, separately budgeted
full-space comparison, followed by system-relevant checks that were absent from
the retained run.

The next chapter asks which parts of the executed array study and its retained
record can be reused when the workload, objective, tool, implementation target,
or system context changes
(@sec-loop-patterns-across-stack).
